title: 8 Best Bulk Calling Software for High-Volume Hiring (2026)
summary: 8 bulk calling platforms rated for high-volume recruiting on dialer speed, ATS integration, compliance, deliverability, and cost per hire.
body_markdown:
## TLDR


-


Recruiters screening candidates across borders: Plivo, the only option here pairing an owned carrier network in 150+ countries with a programmable dialer and SOC 2, GDPR, and HIPAA coverage


-


Teams already standardized on Twilio: Twilio, flexible and battle-tested, but you assemble the recruiting workflow yourself


-


Agencies wanting a dialer plus CRM in one seat: JustCall or PhoneBurner, quick to deploy with power-dialing built in


-


In-house talent teams tied to an ATS: Aircall, deepest catalog of native recruiting integrations


-


Pricing range: $0.004/min (Plivo usage-based voice) to ~$149/user/mo (PhoneBurner seat pricing)


Your recruiting team runs a req that just pulled 4,000 applicants for 60 seasonal warehouse roles. Every one of those candidates needs a screening call in the next ten days, and the phone is still the fastest way to confirm availability, shift preference, and whether they'll actually show up on day one.


Doing that by hand, one number at a time, is where hiring pipelines quietly die. Recruiters spend more of the day listening to ringing and voicemail beeps than they do talking to people. Bulk calling software exists to close that gap: it dials lists automatically, skips dead numbers, and connects a live recruiter only when a human picks up.


But "bulk calling" gets used loosely, and most roundups lump together consumer robocall apps, sales power dialers, and carrier-grade platforms as if they were interchangeable. High-volume hiring has its own requirements: it is outbound-heavy, spiky around seasonal peaks, sensitive to candidate experience, and increasingly bound by consent and calling-time rules that a recruiter cannot afford to get wrong.


This article rates eight voice-capable platforms on the six things recruiting operations actually buy on: dialer mode and connect rate, ATS and CRM integration, telephony ownership, compliance and consent tooling, number deliverability, and total cost per candidate reached.

## What Actually Matters for High-Volume Hiring


Generic dialer comparisons skip the parts recruiting operations live or die on. Here is what to pressure-test on any tool you shortlist:


1. Dialer mode and connect rate. Preview, progressive, power, and predictive dialers all trade off differently between recruiter idle time and dropped-call risk. Predictive dialing maximizes talk time on huge lists but can abandon calls if pacing is aggressive, which reads as a hang-up to a candidate. Ask for the platform's default abandon rate and whether pacing is configurable per campaign.


2. ATS and CRM integration. A dialer that doesn't write call outcomes back to your applicant tracking system creates a second system of record that recruiters have to reconcile by hand. Confirm native, two-way sync with your ATS (Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, Bullhorn) rather than a generic Zapier bridge that breaks under volume.


3. Telephony ownership. Does the vendor own its carrier network or resell someone else's? Reselling adds a latency hop and a second point of failure, and it usually means less control over caller ID reputation, the single biggest driver of whether candidates pick up. Only Plivo and Twilio in this set run their own networks.


4. Compliance and consent tooling. High-volume outbound to candidates touches TCPA calling-window rules, DNC scrubbing, and, for regulated employers, background-check and data-handling obligations. Look for built-in time-zone-aware calling windows, consent capture, and automatic DNC suppression, not a checkbox that pushes the liability onto you.


5. Number deliverability and reputation. Candidates ignore calls that show up as "Spam Likely." Ask whether the platform supports branded caller ID, STIR/SHAKEN attestation, local-presence dialing, and number rotation to keep your outbound numbers from getting flagged mid-campaign.


6. Cost per candidate reached. Seat-based pricing looks simple until a seasonal spike forces you to buy licenses you'll cancel in six weeks. Usage-based per-minute pricing scales with actual volume. Model both against your peak week, not your average one.


## The 8 Best Bulk Calling Platforms for High-Volume Hiring


### 1. Plivo


Best For: High-growth and global recruiting teams that need programmable bulk outbound across many countries on one compliant stack


Plivo is a communications infrastructure company with an owned carrier network reaching 150+ countries, and it exposes that network through a programmable voice API plus a no-code agent studio. For recruiting, that means you can build a dialer that fits your funnel exactly: auto-dial a candidate list, detect voicemail, drop a pre-recorded message, and connect live pickups straight to a recruiter, all on infrastructure the vendor controls end to end.


Because the carrier layer, the call routing, and the compliance stack are one system, caller-ID reputation and calling-window enforcement live in the same place you build the campaign. That single chain-of-custody is what lets a talent team run a 5,000-call screening blitz and still keep a clean audit trail for consent and DNC suppression.


The same platform spans voice, SMS, and WhatsApp with shared context, so a candidate who misses a screening call can get an SMS with a self-schedule link and continue the conversation on WhatsApp without re-explaining who they are.


#### Key Features


-


Owned carrier network in 150+ countries with local numbers and one-hop routing


-


Programmable voice API (Python, Node, Go, REST) plus a no-code studio for non-technical recruiting ops


-


Answering-machine detection, prerecorded voicemail drop, and live-transfer to recruiters


-


Time-zone-aware calling windows and DNC suppression for TCPA-conscious outbound


-


Omnichannel candidate journeys across voice, SMS, and WhatsApp with shared context


-


SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001 with US, EU, and APAC data residency


-


Usage-based per-minute pricing that scales down between seasonal peaks


#### Limitations


-


Not a turnkey recruiting suite out of the box: the ATS write-back and candidate scoring are things you configure, not features you toggle on day one.


-


The full agent platform sits on an enterprise plan, so the lowest tier is aimed at teams with real volume rather than a single recruiter testing the waters.


#### Pricing


Voice starts at $0.004/min on Plivo's network, billed by usage. The AI Agents platform (no-code builder, concurrency, knowledge base, simulation testing) starts at $1,000/month on the Enterprise plan. New accounts get $10 in free credits with no card required.


### 2. Twilio


Best For: Engineering-backed talent teams already standardized on Twilio who want to assemble a bespoke hiring dialer


Twilio is the default building block for programmable communications, and a bulk hiring dialer is well within what its Voice API and Studio flow builder can do. If your team already runs Twilio for candidate SMS or two-factor, extending into automated outbound calling avoids onboarding a new vendor.


The tradeoff is that Twilio hands you components, not a recruiting product. Voicemail detection, list management, ATS sync, and campaign pacing are things you wire together with Twilio primitives and your own code. That is maximum flexibility for teams with developers and unnecessary overhead for teams without them.


#### Key Features


-


Owned telephony network with numbers in 100+ countries


-


Voice API plus Studio drag-and-drop flow builder for call logic


-


Largest integration marketplace in the category across CRM, analytics, and data tools


-


STIR/SHAKEN attestation and branded caller-ID options for deliverability


-


SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001, and HIPAA coverage


-


Deep documentation and a large developer community


#### Limitations


-


No recruiting-native workflow. There is no candidate list view, ATS write-back, or screening template until you build one.


-


Costs are itemized across voice minutes, numbers, add-on AI features, and support tiers, so the all-in per-minute figure is higher than the headline rate suggests.


#### Pricing


Outbound voice starts around $0.014–$0.022/min, phone numbers run $1–$2/month, and AI or intelligence features are billed separately. Paid support starts at $250/month.


### 3. JustCall


Best For: Recruiting agencies and staffing firms that want a dialer, texting, and light CRM in a single seat


What It Does


JustCall packages an auto-dialer, SMS, and call analytics into a business phone product aimed at sales and staffing teams. For agency recruiters working long candidate lists, its sales dialer and predictive dialing keep talk time high without a developer in the loop.


It leans into the recruiting and staffing use case with native Bullhorn and other ATS integrations, so call outcomes and notes can flow back to the system recruiters already live in.


#### Key Features


-


Auto, predictive, and dynamic dialer modes with configurable pacing


-


Native integrations with Bullhorn, HubSpot, and common ATS/CRM tools


-


Bulk SMS and call-and-text campaigns from the same inbox


-


Call recording, transcription, and basic conversation analytics


-


SOC 2, GDPR, and HIPAA coverage


#### Limitations


-


Runs on third-party carriers, so caller-ID reputation and international reach depend on upstream providers.


-


Predictive dialing and higher call volumes sit on the pricier tiers, which adds up quickly across a large recruiting team.


#### Pricing


Seat-based plans run roughly $29–$99/user/month depending on dialer features, with predictive dialing and AI add-ons on the upper tiers.


### 4. Aircall


Best For: In-house talent acquisition teams whose priority is deep, reliable ATS integration


Aircall is a cloud phone system built around integrations, and its strength for hiring is the breadth of native connectors to recruiting tools. Click-to-dial from inside your ATS, automatic call logging, and a power dialer for working through candidate lists come standard rather than as custom work.


It is designed for business users, not developers, so a talent ops manager can set up a screening campaign, assign numbers, and route pickups without engineering support.


#### Key Features


-


Power dialer for sequential list calling with logging


-


Large catalog of native integrations, including major ATS and CRM platforms


-


Numbers available in 100+ countries through carrier partners


-


Shared call inbox, routing rules, and live activity feed for teams


-


SOC 2 and GDPR coverage


#### Limitations


-


No predictive dialing, so raw dials-per-hour trails dedicated power-dialing tools on the very largest lists.


-


No owned carrier network and no HIPAA offering, which can matter for regulated-industry hiring.


#### Pricing


Seat-based plans run roughly $30–$50/user/month, with the power dialer and advanced analytics on higher tiers and a typical three-seat minimum.


### 5. Dialpad


Best For: Recruiting teams that want built-in voice AI, live transcription, and real-time coaching on screening calls


Dialpad pairs a business phone system with voice AI that transcribes calls in real time, surfaces action items, and can coach recruiters live during a conversation. For high-volume screening, the appeal is turning every call into structured, searchable notes automatically instead of asking recruiters to type up outcomes.


Its outbound and power-dialing features handle list calling, while the AI layer captures candidate answers on availability, salary expectation, and start date without manual note-taking.


#### Key Features


-


Real-time transcription and AI call summaries out of the box


-


Power dialer with live-coaching prompts for recruiters


-


Sentiment and keyword tracking across call volume


-


Numbers in 70+ countries through carrier partners


-


SOC 2, GDPR, and HIPAA coverage


#### Limitations


-


Runs on third-party carriers, so international deliverability and caller-ID control are less direct than an owned-network provider.


-


The AI features that justify the platform are strongest in English, with thinner support for other candidate languages.


#### Pricing


Seat-based plans start around $15–$25/user/month, with the AI and power-dialing capabilities concentrated on the mid and upper tiers.


### 6. PhoneBurner


Best For: Agency recruiters who live in a power dialer and want the highest dials-per-hour with zero connection delay


PhoneBurner is a dedicated power dialer built to eliminate the awkward pause between a candidate picking up and a recruiter speaking. It dials from a list one number at a time, drops voicemails with a click, and logs outcomes, and its selling point is a delay-free connection that keeps talk time high and abandon rates effectively nil.


For staffing agencies working through warm candidate lists, that combination of speed and a compliant, human-paced experience is the entire pitch.


#### Key Features


-


Delay-free power dialing with no predictive-abandon risk


-


One-click voicemail drop and email follow-up


-


Built-in contact management with dispositions and cadences


-


Local-presence dialing to lift US/Canada answer rates


-


SOC 2 and GDPR coverage


#### Limitations


-


Power dialing only: no predictive mode, so it prioritizes candidate experience over absolute maximum dials.


-


US and Canada focused, with limited international reach for global hiring.


#### Pricing


Flat seat pricing around $149/user/month, positioned as an all-inclusive power-dialing seat rather than usage-based.


### 7. CloudTalk


Best For: Talent teams running structured outbound campaigns who want smart dialing plus reporting in one tool


CloudTalk is a call-center-style platform with strong outbound campaign tooling: smart dialers, call queues, and detailed agent reporting. For recruiting, it suits teams that treat screening like a managed campaign with targets, dispositions, and performance dashboards.


Its wide international numbering makes it a fit for teams hiring across many markets without stitching together local providers per country.


#### Key Features


-


Smart, power, and predictive dialers with campaign management


-


Numbers available in 160+ countries through partners


-


Detailed call analytics, dispositions, and agent scorecards


-


Integrations with common CRM and helpdesk tools


-


SOC 2 and GDPR coverage


#### Limitations


-


Reselling telephony means caller-ID reputation and quality vary by market and upstream carrier.


-


The recruiting fit is generic call-center tooling adapted to hiring rather than purpose-built for candidate screening.


#### Pricing


Seat-based plans run roughly $25–$50/user/month, with predictive dialing and advanced analytics on higher tiers.


### 8. Twilio Studio + Voice API (Custom Build)


Best For: Engineering-led talent organizations that want a fully custom bulk dialer wired directly into their own systems


For teams with developer capacity, a custom build on Twilio's Voice API and Studio flow builder gives total control: define your own pacing, voicemail logic, consent gates, and ATS write-back exactly as your process requires. Nothing is hidden behind a vendor's product decisions.


This is the same underlying network as the packaged Twilio entry above, but treated as raw infrastructure for a bespoke recruiting dialer rather than an off-the-shelf phone system. It is the most flexible option and the most demanding to maintain.


#### Key Features


-


Fully programmable call flows, pacing, and routing


-


Owned telephony network with numbers in 100+ countries


-


Direct, code-level ATS and data-warehouse integration


-


STIR/SHAKEN and branded caller-ID controls for deliverability


-


SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001, and HIPAA coverage


#### Limitations


-


Requires ongoing engineering ownership; there is no recruiting UI for ops teams to self-serve.


-


Time-to-value is measured in weeks of build, not an afternoon of setup.


#### Pricing


Purely usage-based: voice minutes from ~$0.014/min, numbers at $1–$2/month, plus your own engineering cost to build and maintain the dialer.


## Choosing the Right Platform


The right pick comes down to your hiring volume, how global your candidate pool is, whether you have engineering support, and how tightly the dialer must bind to your ATS.


-


Global volume on one compliant stack: Plivo or Twilio, the only owned-network options here. Plivo gives you the programmable dialer and compliance in one system; Twilio gives you the components to build your own.


-


Agency dialing at maximum talk time: PhoneBurner for delay-free power dialing, or JustCall if you also want texting and CRM in the same seat.


-


ATS-native, business-user friendly: Aircall for the widest catalog of recruiting integrations without engineering work.


-


AI notes and coaching on every screen: Dialpad, which turns calls into structured candidate data automatically.


-


Fully custom, engineering-owned: A Twilio Studio build, if you have developers and want the dialer to match your process exactly.


## The Verdict


For high-volume hiring in 2026, the shortlist narrows fast once you filter for owned telephony, real ATS write-back, and consent tooling that holds up across a seasonal spike. Most tools in this set are strong at one of those and rent the rest.


Plivo is the option where the dialer, the carrier network, and the compliance stack are a single system, which is what lets a talent team run thousands of screening calls, catch the misses with an SMS self-schedule link, and keep one clean audit trail for consent across the whole campaign. Usage-based pricing means the bill tracks your actual peak instead of a seat count you'll cancel afterward. The fastest way to know if it fits your funnel is to run it against a live req.


Whatever you choose, model it against your worst week, not your average one, and insist on connect-rate and deliverability numbers before you sign.
